lender_licence: None found for business purpose. The Residential Mortgage Lending Act (ORC 1322) excludes a loan to buy a dwelling to lease, rent or resell. It applies again if the borrower or immediate family will occupy it (OAC 1301:8-7-02(G), eff. 19 Sep 2025)
broker_licence: Same carve-out: the RMLA mortgage broker registration does not apply to business-purpose loans (OAC 1301:8-7-02(G))
usury: Base cap 8% (ORC 1343.01(A)). Exempt: principal over $100,000; business loans to entities or sole proprietors; real estate loans capped at 8% over the 90-day commercial paper discount rate if no other exemption applies (1343.01(B)(1), (4), (6))
default_interest_late_fees: No statutory cap found for business loans. Not found
prepayment: Residential obligations on 2 or fewer units: up to 1% of original principal in the first 5 years. No penalty on first-lien loans under $75,000 (CPI-adjusted) from brokers or non-bank lenders (ORC 1343.011). "Residential mortgage" is defined by collateral (2 or fewer units), not purpose or occupancy (1343.011(A)(2)), so it appears to reach business-purpose loans [VERIFY]
foreclosure: Judicial only. Six months to two years from filing to sheriff's sale (Ohio Legal Help, secondary). Property cannot sell below two-thirds of appraisal (ORC 2329.20, secondary)
deficiency: Allowed. On a 1-2 family dwelling used as a home or homestead, a deficiency is unenforceable 2 years after sale confirmation (ORC 2329.08). An investor-held house is likely outside that limit [VERIFY]
recent_changes: OAC 1301:8-7-02 rewritten, eff. 19 Sep 2025: sets the business-purpose test, including the "more than half consumer" hybrid rule. No pending bill on BPL found

lender_licence: None found for business purpose. The SAFE Act licenses lenders of "residential mortgage loans" made primarily for personal, family or household use (G.S. 53-244.030(30))
broker_licence: Same scope: SAFE Act broker and loan originator licences cover consumer-purpose residential loans only (G.S. 53-244.030)
usury: Over $25,000: any agreed rate (G.S. 24-1.1(a)(2)). Exempt loans: $300,000 or more, a borrower that is not a natural person, or a non-personal purpose. Any rate and fees; usury claim barred (G.S. 24-9)
default_interest_late_fees: Late fee up to 4% of the late payment, only after 15 days, for loans under 24-1.1 or 24-1.1A (G.S. 24-10.1). It covers only loans governed by 24-1.1 or 24-1.1A. G.S. 24-9 lets exempt-loan parties agree charges in any amount, so the cap appears not to bind exempt loans [VERIFY]. No late fee on single-payment loans (24-10.1(b)(5)). Default interest: Not found
prepayment: No penalty on home loans of $150,000 or less to a natural person, for consumer purposes, secured by a primary residence (G.S. 24-1.1A(b)). Loans of $100,000 or less under 24-1.1: 2% maximum in the first 3 years (G.S. 24-10(b), via ELFA, secondary)
foreclosure: Power of sale before the clerk of superior court, after a notice of hearing served at least 10 days ahead (G.S. 45-21.16). Ten-day upset-bid periods follow the sale. Typically 60-90 days (secondary)
deficiency: Barred on seller purchase-money notes (G.S. 45-21.38) and some primary-residence loans (45-21.38A). Borrower may prove fair value as a defence (45-21.36). Otherwise allowed
recent_changes: SAFE Act modernization (SL 2025-43), eff. 1 Oct 2025: new exemptions, qualifying-individual and branch rules, 45-day notice before foreclosure. The consumer-purpose test is unchanged

lender_licence: None for business purpose. The First Lien Mortgage Lending Act exempts credit primarily for a business, commercial or agricultural purpose (IC 24-4.4-1-202)
broker_licence: Possibly required. The Loan Broker Act covers anyone paid to procure a "residential mortgage loan", and the definition turns on collateral, not purpose (IC 23-2.5-1-14, -34) [VERIFY: whether BPL brokers need a licence]
usury: The Uniform Consumer Credit Code caps consumer loans only (IC 24-4.5). Non-consumer loans: any agreed rate if not unconscionable (secondary). The loansharking statute applies only to consumer loans (IC 35-45-7-3)
default_interest_late_fees: No statutory cap found for non-consumer loans. Not found
prepayment: No statutory limit found for business-purpose loans. Not found
foreclosure: Judicial. No sale until 3 months after the complaint is filed, for mortgages signed on or after 1 Jul 1975 (IC 32-29-7-3). No redemption after the sheriff's sale (secondary)
deficiency: Allowed. Barred if the borrower waives the 3-month wait with the lender's consent (IC 32-29-7-5)
recent_changes: HEA 1336 (2024) amended the Loan Broker Act, eff. 1 Jul 2024. No pending BPL bill found

lender_licence: California Financing Law licence for any finance lender making commercial loans. Real estate may secure loans over $5,000 (DFPI FAQ). Exempt: loans made or arranged by a licensed real estate broker (Fin. Code 22057)
broker_licence: Real estate broker licence (DRE) to solicit or negotiate loans secured by real property (B&P 10131(d)). A CFL broker licence covers brokering to CFL lenders only (DFPI FAQ)
usury: 10% cap for non-exempt lenders (Cal. Const. art. XV). Exempt: real estate loans made or arranged by a licensed broker (Civ. Code 1916.1). Lenders licensed as CFL or residential mortgage lenders are also exempt (secondary)
default_interest_late_fees: Late fee on a single-family owner-occupied dwelling: max 6% of the installment or $5, after 10 days (Civ. Code 2954.4). Default interest on the whole balance before maturity is an unlawful penalty (Garrett 1973; Honchariw 2022)
prepayment: Any 1-4 unit loan may be prepaid; a charge needs a written agreement (Civ. Code 2954.9(a)). Owner-occupied: charges only in the first 5 years, 20% a year free, at most 6 months' interest on the excess (2954.9(b))
foreclosure: Mostly non-judicial trustee's sale. Notice of sale at least 90 days after the notice of default, and sale at least 20 days after that (Civ. Code 2924). Eligible tenants and bidders get a 15/45-day post-sale window on 1-4 units until 1 Jan 2031 (2924m)
deficiency: No deficiency against the borrower after a trustee's sale (CCP 580d). A guarantor stays liable if the guaranty carries Civ. Code 2856 waivers (580d(b); CORE-DOC-05). One-action rule: foreclose before suing on the debt (CCP 726). Purchase-money limits (CCP 580b) [VERIFY: owner-occupied scope]
recent_changes: AB 2116, signed 30 Sep 2026: commercial financing licensing from 1 Jul 2028; real-property-secured deals excluded. SB 1146 (2024) amended Civ. Code 1916.1 and foreclosure rules. AB 1837 (2022) extended the 2924m tenant-buyer process to 1 Jan 2031

lender_licence: None found. The RMLA covers residential loans only. The small loan law covers loans of $5,000 or less (ORC 1321.02)
usury: Same as SLT-OH-01: business loans to entities and loans over $100,000 are exempt (ORC 1343.01(B))
prepayment: No statute found. 1343.011 covers 2 or fewer residential units only
foreclosure: Judicial, as SLT-OH-01. Receiver: allowed where the mortgagor consented in writing, or the property is probably worth less than the debt, plus a risk or default shown (ORC 2735.01(A)(2))
deficiency: Allowed. 2329.08 covers only 1-2 family homes, so it does not apply
recent_changes: OAC 1301:8-7-02 rewritten, eff. 19 Sep 2025: sets the business-purpose test, including the "more than half consumer" hybrid rule. No pending bill on BPL found

lender_licence: None found. The SAFE Act covers consumer-purpose residential loans only [VERIFY: no other NC commercial lender licence]
usury: Same as SLT-NC-01. Loans of $300,000 or more, or to entities, are exempt from rate and fee limits (G.S. 24-9)
default_interest_late_fees: 4% late fee rule applies to loans under 24-1.1; exempt 24-9 loans may agree any fees [VERIFY]
prepayment: Lender and borrower may agree any terms, subject to the $100,000 rule in 24-10(b) (ELFA, secondary)
foreclosure: Power of sale, as SLT-NC-01. Limited receiver available in power of sale or judicial foreclosure, including where the debtor agreed in a signed record; the court still decides (G.S. 1-507.24(f), Commercial Receivership Act, eff. 1 Jan 2021)
deficiency: As SLT-NC-01. The primary-residence bar does not apply
recent_changes: SAFE Act modernization (SL 2025-43), eff. 1 Oct 2025: new exemptions, qualifying-individual and branch rules, 45-day notice before foreclosure. The consumer-purpose test is unchanged

lender_licence: None found. Indiana mortgage lending licences cover dwellings and residential real estate (IC 24-4.4)
broker_licence: None found. The Loan Broker Act covers residential mortgage loans only (IC 23-2.5-1-14)
usury: Not capped for non-consumer loans (secondary); loansharking covers consumer loans only (IC 35-45-7-3)
foreclosure: Judicial, 3-month wait, as SLT-IN-01. Receiver: in a mortgage foreclosure where, among other grounds, the property may not cover the debt or the mortgagor agreed in writing (IC 32-30-5-1); notice needed unless cause shown by affidavit (IC 32-30-5-9)
recent_changes: HEA 1336 (2024) amended the Loan Broker Act, eff. 1 Jul 2024. No pending BPL bill found

lender_licence: CFL licence required for commercial loans unless exempt; DRE-broker exemption as SLT-CA-01. From 1 Jul 2028, AB 2116 adds licensing for small business financing of $500,000 or less, but real-property-secured financing is excluded
usury: 10% cap for non-exempt lenders on non-personal loans; same exemptions (Art. XV; Civ. Code 1916.1)
default_interest_late_fees: Civ. Code 2954.4 does not apply. Default interest on the full balance before maturity is a penalty under Civ. Code 1671 (Honchariw)
prepayment: 2954.9 does not apply above 4 units. Terms are contractual
foreclosure: Non-judicial trustee's sale, or judicial. 2924 timing applies; 2924m does not. Receiver: CCP 564(b)(11) allows one to enforce an assignment of rents; the deed of trust's consent avoids proving irreparable harm (secondary); seeking one is not an "action" under the one-action rule (CCP 564(d)). Non-merger after a deed in lieu: CLTA 107.11 endorsement, needs anti-merger recitals in the deed of trust and note (Stewart guideline)
